what: Hovering a menu link plays a small Lottie beside the text (a bird rises with two flaps, .9s·60fps) once from the start. On release it stops and returns to the first frame — a drawer menu where a little character reacts to each link. On touch screens it plays on press.

options.data: Name of the artwork in window.fxLottie — uses its animationData (also runs on file://)
options.src: Lottie JSON address — when there is no data (http only)
options.host: Ancestor selector that receives the interaction, default parent element
options.loop: If true, repeats while hovering, default is once
options.from: Starts playing from this frame on interaction (default 0) — an icon that uses an earlier frame as its resting image (original Brand cart 11f, My Page 2f).
options.min: Turns off interaction when the window width (px) is narrower than this, default 0
options.idle: If loop, it spins endlessly even normally (stops under reduced motion), and when an interaction starts it replays from the from frame — it does not stop when the interaction ends
options.leave: pause: when the pointer leaves it stops at that frame, and when it returns it resumes from there (it does not go back to the first frame) · finish: even if the pointer leaves it plays one full loop to the end and stops at the first frame, and returning mid-play does not restart from the beginning — default goes back to the first frame · reverse: on enter it plays start→end, on leave end→start backward (both begin by jumping straight to that end frame — brand button arrow)
options.step: For a graphic with same-length variations chained in one file, this is that length (frames) — each time the hand arrives, the next segment plays once from the start and stops on the segment’s last frame (step−1). Ignored if the hand arrives again mid-play, and it runs to the end even if the hand leaves (brand header logo variations, five × 30f)

use: ABOUT — The new image color comes from the consumer’s css as .bird path { fill: var(--kf-accent) }
note: The original artwork JSON isn’t carried over. We use our own newly drawn artwork at the same board size (98×67) and frame count (54f @60fps) (the Brand copy is baked by lottie/make.cjs) · focus plays only when it arrives by keyboard (:focus-visible), so a button pressed with the mouse, which receives focus, doesn’t replay an animation that has already run. It also doesn’t stop when focus leaves while the pointer is still over it
